title: The Maple Street Compost Contamination Dilemma

scenario.title: The Maple Street Compost Contamination Dilemma
scenario.setting: Nestled between the library’s back porch and a row of overgrown tomato plants, Maple Street’s neighborhood compost drop-off consists of three weathered wooden bins tagged with handwritten rules. For 18 months, volunteers Marisol and Jules ran the program without incident, collecting food scraps weekly until a batch of unlabeled dairy waste spoiled nearly 70% of the pile last Tuesday. The resulting foul stench has carried to nearby townhomes, prompting three residents to file formal complaints with the neighborhood association.

characters.name: Marisol Espinoza
characters.tendencies: Insists on sticking strictly to the initial program guidelines to rebuild trust with local residents after the contamination incident

characters.name: Jules Torres
characters.tendencies: Argues that bending the program rules temporarily to add free contamination testing stations will prevent future waste spoilage

characters.name: Clara Hale
characters.tendencies: Demands the compost program be shut down entirely unless immediate, permanent changes are made to eliminate the persistent foul stench

turns.name: Marisol Espinoza
turns.text:
Good afternoon, neighbors stopping by the compost drop today. I wanted to share that all local compost materials collected and accepted here have passed recent contamination tests, so you can safely leave your kitchen scraps without any worry. I’ve also restocked the free, sanitized collection bins for anyone who needs a clean way to transport their scraps.
[Kneeling to stack the labeled, clear compost bins neatly on the wooden drop-off platform, brushing a strand of overgrown tomato vine off the handwritten sign posted to the library porch rail]

turns.name: Jules Torres
turns.text:
"Folks, the last two compost drop-off batches had hidden dairy and meat scraps that turned half the neighborhood pile rank and left us without usable garden soil all spring. We can’t wait for the full council vote to add permanent contamination testing stations—temporarily bending the rules to put up these free, temporary testing stations right here will stop spoiled waste from ruining the pile before it’s too late."
[Grabs a stack of hand-lettered "Test Scraps Here" signs from their canvas tote and prods one against a thick wooden stake holding up the overgrown tomato plants]

turns.name: Clara Hale
turns.text:
That unrelenting, putrid stench from the neighborhood compost program has drifted all the way over here between the library’s back porch and overgrown tomato plants, and it’s making it impossible to enjoy being outside right now. This can’t keep going on without immediate, permanent fixes to fully eliminate that foul smell—otherwise, I’m leading the push to shut the entire compost drop-off program down permanently.
[Grabs a crumpled stack of signed neighborhood complaint forms and slams them hard against the side of the compost bin]

turns.name: Marisol Espinoza
turns.text:
I am deeply sorry for the putrid stench that’s drifted through this neighborhood from the contaminated compost piles—this was a mistake on my part for not enforcing clear drop-off rules strictly enough. We’ve now set up clearly marked, dedicated bins only for plant-based scraps and posted large signs right by the porch so everyone knows what’s allowed. I’m here to answer any questions or help you sort your materials correctly today.
[kneels to adjust a crinkled bright green “NO ANIMAL PRODUCTS” sign hanging above the new compost bins, while passing a printed quick-reference sheet to a nearby resident glancing at the posted rules]

turns.name: Jules Torres
turns.text:
"Look, we can’t keep ignoring the hidden contaminated scraps ruining our compost pile—this stench isn’t just unpleasant, it’s wasting the nutrient-rich soil we all rely on for our gardens. We need to temporarily bend the program’s strict rules to set up free on-site contamination testing stations right here at the drop-off, so neighbors can check their scraps without extra cost or hassle, and stop this spoilage before it gets worse."
[Kneels down, pulls a stack of handwritten test station signs from their work bag, and tapes one to the side of the library’s back porch railing to alert passersby.]

turns.name: Clara Hale
turns.text:
That unrelenting, putrid stench from the neighborhood compost program has drifted all the way over here between the library’s back porch and overgrown tomato plants, seeping into the peaceful afternoon air I was enjoying while walking home from the library. Either you make immediate, permanent changes to eliminate this foul stench entirely, or shut the entire compost program down right now. I won’t tolerate this rank odor ruining our neighborhood’s quiet spaces.
[Clutching her frayed canvas library bag tight while swatting at the air repeatedly in front of her nose to dodge the acrid smell]

dm_opening: DM opening: the Marisol Espinoza takes a position; the cast gathers around a question the scene has been carrying for a year.
dm_closing: DM closing: the Marisol Espinoza still holds the line; the next session's hook — a new member, an old scar — is already at the door.
